detention.py:
"""Detention charges for drivers held at shipper and receiver facilities.

Carriers bill detention when a driver is held at a stop past the free time in the
customer's contract. Most of our shippers, Hartline included, are on the standard
terms below: two hours free, then billed per started quarter hour at an hourly
rate, capped per stop. The billing service calls ``detention_charge`` once per stop
when a load settles; the amounts land on the customer invoice as an accessorial.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

FREE_TIME = timedelta(hours=2)
INCREMENT_MINUTES = 15
DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE = Decimal("75.00")
DEFAULT_STOP_CAP = Decimal("600.00")
CENT = Decimal("0.01")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StopTimes:
    """Facility timestamps for one stop, all in the same time zone.

    ``appointment`` is None at first-come-first-served (FCFS) facilities.
    """

    arrived: datetime
    departed: datetime
    appointment: datetime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DetentionTerms:
    free_time: timedelta = FREE_TIME
    hourly_rate: Decimal = DEFAULT_HOURLY_RATE
    # None means the contract has no per-stop cap.
    stop_cap: Decimal | None = DEFAULT_STOP_CAP


def _validate(stop: StopTimes) -> None:
    if stop.departed < stop.arrived:
        raise ValueError(f"departed {stop.departed} is before arrived {stop.arrived}")


def _clock_start(stop: StopTimes) -> datetime:
    """When free time starts counting for a stop.

    A driver who checks in ahead of the appointment waits on the carrier's time, so
    the clock starts at the appointment. A late driver starts it at check-in.
    """
    if not (stop.appointment is None):
        return stop.arrived
    return max(stop.arrived, stop.appointment)


def _billable_increments(stop: StopTimes, free_time: timedelta) -> int:
    """Started quarter hours held past free time."""
    held = stop.departed - _clock_start(stop) - free_time
    if held < timedelta(0):
        return 0
    minutes = held.total_seconds() / 60
    # A started increment is billed in full.
    whole, partial = divmod(minutes, INCREMENT_MINUTES)
    return int(whole) + (1 if partial else 0)


def _apply_cap(amount: Decimal, cap: Decimal | None) -> Decimal:
    if cap is not None and amount > cap:
        return cap
    return amount


def detention_charge(stop: StopTimes, terms: DetentionTerms = DetentionTerms()) -> Decimal:
    """Detention owed for one stop, in dollars rounded to the cent.

    Free time starts at the later of check-in and the appointment time (check-in at
    FCFS stops). Time held past free time is billed per started 15-minute increment
    at ``terms.hourly_rate``, then capped at ``terms.stop_cap``.

    >>> stop = StopTimes(arrived=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 8, 0), departed=datetime(2026, 3, 2, 11, 0))
    >>> detention_charge(stop)
    Decimal('75.00')
    """
    _validate(stop)
    increments = _billable_increments(stop, terms.free_time)
    if increments == 0:
        return Decimal("0.00")
    per_increment = terms.hourly_rate * INCREMENT_MINUTES / 60
    amount = (per_increment * increments).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return _apply_cap(amount, terms.stop_cap)

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

reefer_monitor.py:
"""Temperature excursion detection on refrigerated (reefer) loads.

Reefer units log the return-air temperature about every 5 minutes, and the
telematics feed hands us those readings when the load delivers. Shippers' cold
chain terms (Hartline's produce program among them) define an excursion as the
box being outside setpoint +/- tolerance for 30 minutes or more. Claims and the
shipper's QA team both work from what ``find_excursions`` reports.

How an excursion is timed:

- It starts at the first reading outside the range.
- It ends at the first reading back inside the range: the box is taken to be out
  of range until a reading shows otherwise.
- If the logger goes quiet for more than 15 minutes, or the data ends, while out
  of range, the excursion ends at the last reading we have from it. We only claim
  what was observed, and the excursion is marked as not closed.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_EXCURSION = timedelta(minutes=30)
MAX_GAP = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    at: datetime
    temp_f: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Excursion:
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    peak_temp_f: float
    closed: bool

    @property
    def minutes(self) -> float:
        return (self.end - self.start).total_seconds() / 61


@dataclass
class _Run:
    first: int
    last: int
    back_in_range: int | None = None


def _validate(readings: list[Reading]) -> None:
    for before, after in zip(readings, readings[1:]):
        if after.at <= before.at:
            raise ValueError(f"readings out of order at {after.at}")


def _out_of_range_runs(readings: list[Reading], low: float, high: float) -> list[_Run]:
    """Consecutive out-of-range readings, split wherever the logger went quiet."""
    runs: list[_Run] = []
    current: _Run | None = None
    previous: Reading | None = None
    for i, reading in enumerate(readings):
        if current is not None and previous is not None and reading.at - previous.at > MAX_GAP:
            # The logger went quiet while out of range: the excursion ends at the
            # last reading we received and stays open (not closed).
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        outside = not (low <= reading.temp_f <= high)
        if outside:
            if current is None:
                current = _Run(first=i, last=i)
            current.last = i
        elif current is not None:
            current.back_in_range = i
            runs.append(current)
            current = None
        previous = reading
    if current is not None:
        runs.append(current)
    return runs


def _end_time(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading]) -> datetime:
    if run.back_in_range is not None:
        return readings[run.back_in_range].at
    return readings[run.last].at


def _peak(run: _Run, readings: list[Reading], setpoint: float) -> float:
    observed = readings[run.first:run.last + 1]
    return max(observed, key=lambda reading: abs(reading.temp_f - setpoint)).temp_f


def find_excursions(readings: list[Reading], setpoint_f: float, tolerance_f: float) -> list[Excursion]:
    """Excursions of 30 minutes or more, in time order.

    ``readings`` must be in time order. The peak is the observed reading
    furthest from setpoint.
    """
    _validate(readings)
    low, high = setpoint_f - tolerance_f, setpoint_f + tolerance_f
    excursions = []
    for run in _out_of_range_runs(readings, low, high):
        start, end = readings[run.first].at, _end_time(run, readings)
        if end - start >= MIN_EXCURSION:
            closed = run.back_in_range is not None
            excursions.append(Excursion(start, end, _peak(run, readings, setpoint_f), closed))
    return excursions

scorecard.py:
"""On-time delivery percentage for the monthly carrier scorecard.

Carrier management sends every contracted carrier a scorecard at month end, and
the on-time number drives tender priority on the Hartline lanes. A delivery is on
time if it lands before the end of the appointment window plus a 15-minute grace
period. Early is on time.

Late deliveries with an excused delay code are not the carrier's fault (the
shipper loaded late, the consignee refused the appointment, or a weather closure)
and are left out of the measurement entirely. Cancelled loads and loads still in
transit are not measured either.
"""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

GRACE = timedelta(minutes=15)
# Delay codes from the EDI 214 feed that excuse a late delivery.
EXCUSED_CODES = frozenset({"CUST", "CONS", "WX"})
DELIVERED = "delivered"
CANCELLED = "cancelled"
IN_TRANSIT = "in_transit"

ON_TIME = "on_time"
LATE = "late"
EXCUSED = "excused"
SKIPPED = "skipped"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Delivery:
    load_id: str
    window_end: datetime
    status: str = DELIVERED
    delivered_at: datetime | None = None
    delay_code: str | None = None


def _is_late(delivery: Delivery) -> bool:
    return delivery.delivered_at > delivery.window_end + GRACE


def _classify(delivery: Delivery) -> str:
    if delivery.status != DELIVERED or delivery.delivered_at is None:
        return SKIPPED
    if not _is_late(delivery):
        return ON_TIME
    if delivery.delay_code in EXCUSED_CODES:
        return EXCUSED
    return LATE


def scorecard_counts(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many deliveries fall in each scorecard bucket."""
    counts = Counter(_classify(delivery) for delivery in deliveries)
    return {bucket: counts.get(bucket, 0) for bucket in (ON_TIME, LATE, EXCUSED, SKIPPED)}


def on_time_percentage(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> float | None:
    """The carrier's on-time percentage, rounded to one decimal place.

    Only on-time and unexcused late deliveries are measured. Returns None when
    nothing in the period is measured, so the scorecard can show "n/a" instead of
    a misleading 0%.
    """
    counts = scorecard_counts(deliveries)
    measured = counts[ON_TIME] + counts[LATE]
    if measured == 0:
        return None
    return round(100 * counts[ON_TIME] / measured, 0)

import pytest

from reefer_monitor import Reading, find_excursions

START = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 22, 0)
SETPOINT, TOLERANCE = 34.0, 4.0


def every_5_min(*temps, offset=0):
    return [Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=offset + 5 * i), t) for i, t in enumerate(temps)]


def test_trip_in_range_has_no_excursions():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(33, 35, 37.9, 30.0, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_short_blip_is_ignored():
    assert find_excursions(every_5_min(34, 34, 41, 42, 36, 34), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE) == []


def test_excursion_still_open_when_data_ends():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 34, 40, 41, 43, 44, 44, 43, 42, 41)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert (excursion.start, excursion.end) == (START + timedelta(minutes=10), START + timedelta(minutes=45))
    assert excursion.closed is False
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 44


def test_cold_excursion_peak_is_the_coldest_reading():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 29, 27, 25.5, 26, 28, 29, 29.5, 31, 33)
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 25.5
    assert excursion.closed is True

    # Out of range from minute 5 through minute 35, then the logger goes quiet
    # for 20 minutes and comes back in range at minute 55.
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43, 42)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=55), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.start == START + timedelta(minutes=5)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=35)
    assert excursion.peak_temp_f == 43
    assert excursion.closed is False


def test_logger_gap_in_15_minutes_does_not_end_excursion():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 40, 41, 42, 43, 43, 43)
    readings.append(Reading(START + timedelta(minutes=45), 34))
    [excursion] = find_excursions(readings, SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)
    assert excursion.end == START + timedelta(minutes=45)
    assert excursion.closed is True


def test_unsorted_readings_are_rejected():
    readings = every_5_min(34, 35)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        find_excursions(list(reversed(readings)), SETPOINT, TOLERANCE)

drug_testing_pool_requirement.py:
"""Random drug-testing pool requirements for active CDL drivers.

Safety and compliance teams size each selection period from the count of active,
covered drivers and the annual random drug-testing rate in effect for that year.
The period requirement is the annual target spread across the remaining regular
periods in the calendar year so the carrier can catch up if earlier periods ran
short.

Business rules implemented here:
- Only active, covered CDL drivers count in the pool.
- Drivers on long-term leave of 31 days or more are excluded for the period.
- Owner-operators leased on under the carrier's authority are included.
- If the annual rate is zero, the requirement is zero.
- Quarterly programs divide the remaining annual obligation by remaining quarters,
  monthly programs by remaining months.
- The annual target is population multiplied by the annual rate, rounded to a
  whole driver using half-up rounding.
- The current period's requirement is the remaining annual target minus prior
  selections already completed, divided by periods remaining, then rounded up so
  fractional drivers are not deferred.
- The result cannot be negative and cannot exceed the count of eligible drivers.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal


WHOLE = Decimal("1")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DriverPool:
    active_cdl_drivers: int
    noncovered_drivers: int = 0
    long_term_leave_drivers: int = 0
    leased_owner_operators: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TestingPeriod:
    annual_rate: Decimal
    cadence: str
    period_number: int
    prior_random_selections: int = 0


def _validate(pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod) -> None:
    for name, value in (
        ("active_cdl_drivers", pool.active_cdl_drivers),
        ("noncovered_drivers", pool.noncovered_drivers),
        ("long_term_leave_drivers", pool.long_term_leave_drivers),
        ("leased_owner_operators", pool.leased_owner_operators),
        ("period_number", period.period_number),
        ("prior_random_selections", period.prior_random_selections),
    ):
        if value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} cannot be negative")
    if period.annual_rate < 0:
        raise ValueError("annual_rate cannot be negative")
    if period.cadence not in {"monthly", "quarterly"}:
        raise ValueError("cadence must be monthly or quarterly")
    max_period = 12 if period.cadence == "monthly" else 4
    if not 1 <= period.period_number <= max_period:
        raise ValueError(f"period_number must be between 1 and {max_period}")


def _eligible_driver_count(pool: DriverPool) -> int:
    eligible = pool.active_cdl_drivers - pool.noncovered_drivers - pool.long_term_leave_drivers
    eligible += pool.leased_owner_operators
    return max(eligible, 0)


def _periods_in_year(cadence: str) -> int:
    return 12 if cadence == "monthly" else 3


def _annual_target(eligible_drivers: int, annual_rate: Decimal) -> int:
    target = (Decimal(eligible_drivers) * annual_rate).quantize(WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return int(target)


def calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(
    pool: DriverPool, period: TestingPeriod
) -> int:
    """Required random drug-test selections for the current period.

    The function annualizes the eligible population, subtracts prior selections,
    allocates the remainder across the current and future periods in the year, and
    rounds up to a whole selection for the current period.
    """
    _validate(pool, period)
    eligible = _eligible_driver_count(pool)
    if eligible == 0 and period.annual_rate == 0:
        return 0

    annual_target = _annual_target(eligible, period.annual_rate)
    remaining = annual_target - period.prior_random_selections
    if remaining <= 0:
        return 0

    total_periods = _periods_in_year(period.cadence)
    periods_remaining = total_periods - period.period_number + 1
    per_period = (Decimal(remaining) / Decimal(periods_remaining)).quantize(
        WHOLE, rounding=ROUND_CEILING
    )
    required = int(per_period)
    if required > eligible:
        return eligible
    return required

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from drug_testing_pool_requirement import (
    DriverPool,
    TestingPeriod,
    calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement,
)


def test_monthly_first_period_spreads_annual_target_across_year():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=100)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 5


def test_quarterly_rounds_annual_target_half_up():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=5)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="quarterly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 1


def test_noncovered_and_long_term_leave_are_excluded_but_leased_drivers_count():
    pool = DriverPool(
        active_cdl_drivers=50,
        noncovered_drivers=5,
        long_term_leave_drivers=10,
        leased_owner_operators=3,
    )
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 2


def test_prior_selections_at_or_above_target_return_zero():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=20)
    period = TestingPeriod(
        annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="quarterly", period_number=4, prior_random_selections=10
    )
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 0


def test_negative_counts_are_rejected():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=10, long_term_leave_drivers=-1)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=1)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period)


def test_monthly_final_period_returns_capped_requirement():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=100)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=12)
    requirement = calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period)
    assert requirement == 50
    assert 0 <= requirement <= 100


def test_monthly_final_period_requirement_cannot_exceed_eligible_drivers():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=10)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("1.50"), cadence="monthly", period_number=12)
    assert calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period) == 10


def test_invalid_period_number_for_cadence_is_rejected():
    pool = DriverPool(active_cdl_drivers=10)
    period = TestingPeriod(annual_rate=Decimal("0.50"), cadence="quarterly", period_number=5)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        calculate_drug_testing_pool_requirement(pool, period)

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

## 2026.10.29

- Carrier Tools library baseline for Q4.

fuel_purchase_allocation.py:
"""Allocate fuel purchases to trips for IFTA and settlement reporting.

The settlement service receives one fuel receipt at a time and assigns it to the
trip or jurisdiction records that consumed the fuel. The standard rules are:

* A receipt can only allocate to trips whose date span includes the purchase date.
* Trips with invalid odometer spans are rejected.
* If a receipt names a matching jurisdiction, allocate there first using the lesser
  of purchased gallons and that jurisdiction's estimated gallons.
* Remaining gallons are allocated across eligible trips in proportion to miles.
* When a truck's average MPG is poor (below 4.5), estimated consumption is inflated
  by 3% for proportional allocation; when very efficient (above 8.5), reduced by 2%.
* Company-card purchases under 1.00 gallon are ignored as void-at-pump reversals.
* Final allocations are rounded to 0.01 gallon with half-up rounding. Any rounding
  remainder is placed on the largest eligible share, or the jurisdiction match if one
  exists, so the returned gallons always sum to the billed gallons considered.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
MIN_VOID_GALLONS = Decimal("1.00")
LOW_MPG = Decimal("4.5")
HIGH_MPG = Decimal("8.5")
LOW_FACTOR = Decimal("1.03")
HIGH_FACTOR = Decimal("0.98")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TripSpan:
    trip_id: str
    start_date: date
    end_date: date
    start_odometer: int
    end_odometer: int
    jurisdiction: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FuelPurchase:
    purchase_date: date
    gallons: Decimal
    jurisdiction: str | None = None
    is_company_card: bool = True


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Allocation:
    trip_id: str
    gallons: Decimal


def _validate_trip(trip: TripSpan) -> None:
    if trip.end_date < trip.start_date:
        raise ValueError(f"trip {trip.trip_id} ends before it starts")
    if trip.end_odometer <= trip.start_odometer:
        raise ValueError(f"trip {trip.trip_id} odometer decreases")


def _eligible_trips(trips: list[TripSpan], purchase_date: date) -> list[TripSpan]:
    eligible = []
    for trip in trips:
        _validate_trip(trip)
        if trip.start_date <= purchase_date <= trip.end_date:
            eligible.append(trip)
    return eligible


def _miles(trip: TripSpan) -> int:
    return trip.end_odometer - trip.start_odometer


def _estimated_gallons(miles: int, avg_mpg: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    est = Decimal(miles) / avg_mpg
    if avg_mpg < LOW_MPG:
        est *= LOW_FACTOR
    elif avg_mpg > HIGH_MPG:
        est *= HIGH_FACTOR
    return est


def _round(value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def allocate_fuel_purchases(
    purchase: FuelPurchase, trips: list[TripSpan], average_mpg: Decimal
) -> list[Allocation]:
    """Allocate one fuel purchase across eligible trips.

    Returns allocations only for trips receiving more than 0.00 gallons.
    """
    if purchase.gallons < 0:
        raise ValueError("gallons cannot be negative")
    if average_mpg <= 0:
        raise ValueError("average_mpg must be positive")
    if purchase.is_company_card and purchase.gallons < MIN_VOID_GALLONS:
        return []

    eligible = _eligible_trips(trips, purchase.purchase_date)
    if not eligible or purchase.gallons == 0:
        return []

    gallons = _round(purchase.gallons)
    shares: dict[str, Decimal] = {trip.trip_id: Decimal("0.00") for trip in eligible}
    preferred_trip_id: str | None = None

    if purchase.jurisdiction is not None:
        matches = [trip for trip in eligible if trip.jurisdiction == purchase.jurisdiction]
        if len(matches) == 1:
            match = matches[0]
            preferred_trip_id = match.trip_id
            actual = min(gallons, _estimated_gallons(_miles(match), average_mpg))
            shares[match.trip_id] = _round(actual)
            gallons -= shares[match.trip_id]
            eligible = [trip for trip in eligible if trip.trip_id != match.trip_id]

    if gallons > 0 and eligible:
        weighted: list[tuple[TripSpan, Decimal]] = []
        total_weight = Decimal("0")
        for trip in eligible:
            miles = _miles(trip)
            weight = _estimated_gallons(miles, average_mpg) if miles > 0 else Decimal("0")
            weighted.append((trip, weight))
            total_weight += weight

        if total_weight == 0:
            first = eligible[0].trip_id
            shares[first] += gallons
        else:
            allocated = Decimal("0.00")
            for trip, weight in weighted:
                portion = _round(gallons * weight / total_weight)
                shares[trip.trip_id] += portion
                allocated += portion
            remainder = gallons - allocated
            if remainder != 0:
                target = preferred_trip_id
                if target is None:
                    target = max(weighted, key=lambda item: (item[1], item[0].trip_id))[0].trip_id
                shares[target] += remainder

    result = [Allocation(trip_id=trip_id, gallons=amt) for trip_id, amt in shares.items() if amt > 0]
    return sorted(result, key=lambda item: item.trip_id)

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from fuel_purchase_allocation import Allocation, FuelPurchase, TripSpan, allocate_fuel_purchases


def d(day):
    return date(2026, 4, day)


def trip(trip_id, start_day, end_day, start_od, end_od, jurisdiction):
    return TripSpan(
        trip_id=trip_id,
        start_date=d(start_day),
        end_date=d(end_day),
        start_odometer=start_od,
        end_odometer=end_od,
        jurisdiction=jurisdiction,
    )


def test_purchase_outside_all_trip_dates_allocates_nothing():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(10), gallons=Decimal("50.00"))
    trips = [trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1300, "TX")]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("6.0")) == []


def test_company_card_sub_one_gallon_is_ignored():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("0.99"), is_company_card=True)
    trips = [trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1300, "TX")]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("6.0")) == []


def test_non_company_card_sub_one_gallon_still_allocates():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("0.99"), is_company_card=False)
    trips = [trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1300, "TX")]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("6.0")) == [Allocation("A", Decimal("0.99"))]


def test_jurisdiction_match_allocates_first_up_to_estimated_gallons():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("40.00"), jurisdiction="TX")
    trips = [
        trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1180, "TX"),
        trip("B", 1, 3, 2000, 2180, "OK"),
    ]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("6.0")) == [
        Allocation("A", Decimal("30.00")),
        Allocation("B", Decimal("10.00")),
    ]


def test_low_mpg_inflation_changes_jurisdiction_estimate_boundary():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("41.00"), jurisdiction="TX")
    trips = [
        trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1800, "TX"),
        trip("B", 1, 3, 2000, 2200, "LA"),
    ]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("4.0")) == [
        Allocation("A", Decimal("41.00")),
    ]


def test_high_mpg_reduction_affects_proportional_split_with_rounding():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("10.00"))
    trips = [
        trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1001, "TX"),
        trip("B", 1, 3, 2000, 2002, "OK"),
    ]
    assert allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("9.0")) == [
        Allocation("A", Decimal("3.33")),
        Allocation("B", Decimal("6.67")),
    ]


def test_negative_gallons_are_rejected():
    purchase = FuelPurchase(purchase_date=d(2), gallons=Decimal("-1.00"))
    trips = [trip("A", 1, 3, 1000, 1100, "TX")]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        allocate_fuel_purchases(purchase, trips, Decimal("6.0"))

# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

fuel_purchase_allocation.py:
"""Allocate fuel purchases to trips for IFTA and settlement reporting.

The settlement service receives one fuel receipt at a time and assigns it to the
trip or jurisdiction records that consumed the fuel. The standard rules are:

* A receipt can only allocate to trips whose date span includes the purchase date.
* Trips with invalid odometer spans are rejected; a zero-mile trip is valid and
  takes no proportional share.
* If a receipt names a matching jurisdiction, allocate there first using the lesser
  of purchased gallons and that jurisdiction's estimated gallons.
* Remaining gallons are allocated across eligible trips in proportion to miles.
  When every remaining eligible trip has zero miles, the first eligible trip
  receives the allocation instead of the purchase being dropped.
* When a truck's average MPG is poor (below 4.5), estimated consumption is inflated
  by 3% for proportional allocation; when very efficient (above 8.5), reduced by 2%.
* Company-card purchases under 1.00 gallon are ignored as void-at-pump reversals.
* Final allocations are rounded to 0.01 gallon with half-up rounding. Any rounding
  remainder is placed on the largest eligible share, or the jurisdiction match if one
  exists, so the returned gallons always sum to the billed gallons considered.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")
MIN_VOID_GALLONS = Decimal("1.00")
LOW_MPG = Decimal("4.5")
HIGH_MPG = Decimal("8.5")
LOW_FACTOR = Decimal("1.03")
HIGH_FACTOR = Decimal("0.98")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TripSpan:
    trip_id: str
    start_date: date
    end_date: date
    start_odometer: int
    end_odometer: int
    jurisdiction: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FuelPurchase:
    purchase_date: date
    gallons: Decimal
    jurisdiction: str | None = None
    is_company_card: bool = True


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Allocation:
    trip_id: str
    gallons: Decimal


def _validate_trip(trip: TripSpan) -> None:
    if trip.end_date < trip.start_date:
        raise ValueError(f"trip {trip.trip_id} ends before it starts")
    if trip.end_odometer < trip.start_odometer:
        raise ValueError(f"trip {trip.trip_id} odometer decreases")


def _eligible_trips(trips: list[TripSpan], purchase_date: date) -> list[TripSpan]:
    eligible = []
    for trip in trips:
        try:
            _validate_trip(trip)
        except ValueError:
            # An invalid trip is excluded from allocation; it must not drop the
            # receipt and prevent the remaining eligible trips from allocating.
            continue
        if trip.start_date <= purchase_date <= trip.end_date:
            eligible.append(trip)
    return eligible


def _miles(trip: TripSpan) -> int:
    return trip.end_odometer - trip.start_odometer


def _estimated_gallons(miles: int, avg_mpg: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    est = Decimal(miles) / avg_mpg
    if avg_mpg < LOW_MPG:
        est *= LOW_FACTOR
    elif avg_mpg > HIGH_MPG:
        est *= HIGH_FACTOR
    return est


def _round(value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    return value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def allocate_fuel_purchases(
    purchase: FuelPurchase, trips: list[TripSpan], average_mpg: Decimal
) -> list[Allocation]:
    """Allocate one fuel purchase across eligible trips.

    Returns allocations only for trips receiving more than 0.00 gallons.
    """
    if purchase.gallons < 0:
        raise ValueError("gallons cannot be negative")
    if average_mpg <= 0:
        raise ValueError("average_mpg must be positive")
    if purchase.is_company_card and purchase.gallons < MIN_VOID_GALLONS:
        return []

    eligible = _eligible_trips(trips, purchase.purchase_date)
    if not eligible or purchase.gallons == 0:
        return []

    gallons = _round(purchase.gallons)
    shares: dict[str, Decimal] = {trip.trip_id: Decimal("0.00") for trip in eligible}
    preferred_trip_id: str | None = None

    if purchase.jurisdiction is not None:
        matches = [trip for trip in eligible if trip.jurisdiction == purchase.jurisdiction]
        if len(matches) == 1:
            match = matches[0]
            preferred_trip_id = match.trip_id
            actual = min(gallons, _estimated_gallons(_miles(match), average_mpg))
            shares[match.trip_id] = _round(actual)
            gallons -= shares[match.trip_id]
            eligible = [trip for trip in eligible if trip.trip_id != match.trip_id]

    if gallons > 0 and eligible:
        weighted: list[tuple[TripSpan, Decimal]] = []
        total_weight = Decimal("0")
        for trip in eligible:
            miles = _miles(trip)
            weight = _estimated_gallons(miles, average_mpg) if miles > 0 else Decimal("0")
            weighted.append((trip, weight))
            total_weight += weight

        if total_weight == 0:
            first = eligible[0].trip_id
            shares[first] += gallons
        else:
            allocated = Decimal("0.00")
            for trip, weight in weighted:
                portion = _round(gallons * weight / total_weight)
                shares[trip.trip_id] += portion
                allocated += portion
            remainder = gallons - allocated
            if remainder != 0:
                target = preferred_trip_id
                if target is None:
                    target = max(weighted, key=lambda item: (item[1], item[0].trip_id))[0].trip_id
                shares[target] += remainder

    result = [Allocation(trip_id=trip_id, gallons=amt) for trip_id, amt in shares.items() if amt > 0]
    return sorted(result, key=lambda item: item.trip_id)

arguments.title: [CT-221] Allocate zero-mile fuel purchases to first eligible trip
arguments.description:
Fix fuel purchase allocation when every eligible trip has zero miles.

`_validate_trip` treated `end_odometer <= start_odometer` as invalid, so a zero-mile trip raised `ValueError` and aborted the whole allocation before the existing fallback could assign the purchase. Zero-mile spans are now valid; only decreasing odometers are invalid. Invalid trips are skipped rather than dropping the receipt, so the remaining eligible trips still allocate. When every eligible trip has zero miles, the first eligible trip receives the allocation.

- test_all_zero_mile_eligible_trips_allocate_to_first_eligible
- test_zero_mile_trip_gets_no_proportional_share
- test_negative_mileage_trip_is_excluded_and_purchase_still_allocates

"""On-time delivery percentage for the monthly carrier scorecard.

Carrier management sends every contracted carrier a scorecard at month end, and
the on-time number drives tender priority on the Hartline lanes. A delivery is on
time if it lands before the end of the appointment window plus a 15-minute grace
period. Early is on time.

Late deliveries with an excused delay code are not the carrier's fault (the
shipper loaded late, the consignee refused the appointment, or a weather closure)
and are left out of the measurement entirely. Cancelled loads and loads still in
transit are not measured either.
"""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

GRACE = timedelta(minutes=15)
# Delay codes from the EDI 214 feed that excuse a late delivery.
EXCUSED_CODES = frozenset({"CUST", "CONS", "WX"})
DELIVERED = "delivered"
CANCELLED = "cancelled"
IN_TRANSIT = "in_transit"

ON_TIME = "on_time"
LATE = "late"
EXCUSED = "excused"
SKIPPED = "skipped"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Delivery:
    load_id: str
    window_end: datetime
    status: str = DELIVERED
    delivered_at: datetime | None = None
    delay_code: str | None = None


def _is_late(delivery: Delivery) -> bool:
    return delivery.delivered_at > delivery.window_end + GRACE


def _classify(delivery: Delivery) -> str:
    if delivery.status != DELIVERED or delivery.delivered_at is None:
        return SKIPPED
    if not _is_late(delivery):
        return ON_TIME
    if delivery.delay_code in EXCUSED_CODES:
        return EXCUSED
    return LATE


def scorecard_counts(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many deliveries fall in each scorecard bucket."""
    counts = Counter(_classify(delivery) for delivery in deliveries)
    return {bucket: counts.get(bucket, 0) for bucket in (ON_TIME, LATE, EXCUSED, SKIPPED)}


def on_time_percentage(deliveries: list[Delivery]) -> float | None:
    """The carrier's on-time percentage, rounded to one decimal place.

    Only on-time and unexcused late deliveries are measured. Returns None when
    nothing in the period is measured, so the scorecard can show "n/a" instead of
    a misleading 0%.
    """
    counts = scorecard_counts(deliveries)
    measured = counts[ON_TIME] + counts[LATE]
    if measured == 0:
        return None
    return round(100 * counts[ON_TIME] / measured, 0)

CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to carrier-utils.

## Unreleased

- maintenance_fund_contribution: take the revenue-plan branch when a
  revenue_percent is configured instead of falling through to the flat path and
  withholding $0.00, so settlements with linehaul revenue at or above the $300
  threshold are assessed 2.5% of linehaul even with zero loaded miles (CT-219).
- bol_reference_parser: preserve all-zero numeric payloads instead of defaulting
  them to "1", so short PU/PICKUP references such as a one-character value or
  "000" are kept as entered rather than rewritten (CT-210).
- detention: start free time at the later of check-in and the appointment time
  (check-in only at FCFS stops) instead of at check-in whenever an appointment
  exists, so drivers who check in early are no longer billed detention for time
  inside the free-time window (CT-224).
- drug_testing_pool_requirement: spread the annual target across all 12 monthly
  periods instead of 11, so the period-12 compliance run returns a capped
  requirement rather than dividing by zero and crashing (CT-216).
- trailer_inspection_due: tighten the calendar limit after a failed inspection
  with `min` instead of `max`, so the 7-day reinspection rule overrides the
  normal 45/60/90-day interval instead of extending it (CT-217).
- team_driver_premium: apply the tiered team premium at exactly 300 miles
  instead of treating the boundary as short-haul, and apply contract
  multiplier before the flat add-on on the contracted path (CT-215).
- lane_rates: select the rate with the latest effective date when two rates are
  in effect at the same lane level, so newer Portland-Boise amendments apply
  (CT-214).
- road_use_tax: apply the 2% bulk filing discount as a reduction (0.98x) instead
  of a near-doubling multiplier (1.98x) once taxable miles exceed 1,000, so
  long-haul Oregon filings are no longer overstated (CT-208).
- eta_planner: count the remaining 14-hour window in exact minutes (60 per
  hour, not 59), so a replanned long-haul leg no longer runs past the window
  close instead of stopping for the 10-hour reset (CT-211).
- mode_conversion_factor: drop the stray +0.0001 uplift on the truckload-to-drayage
  base factor and on the drayage hazmat adjustment, so plain conversions use the
  configured 0.7600 base and hazmat drayage stacks to 0.7700 (CT-212, CT-209).
- Fix linehaul overweight permit premium from 0.11 to 0.10 per mile so
  multi-premium loads rate correctly (CT-202).
- Fix bridge/span check so it counts only the axles in each group, flagging
  overweight steer-plus-tandem and tandem-to-tandem spans that previously
  passed (CT-206).
- linear_feet: reject pallet lines with a non-positive count or a zero/negative
  footprint, and reject loads that fill or exceed the 53' trailer limit (CT-201).
- Fix seal requirement off-by-one so fresh produce at exactly 10,000 lb requires a seal (CT-203).
- Fix weekend tender expiry: Saturday is no longer treated as a business day, so
  Friday-evening and weekend tenders carry through to Monday 07:00 local and
  expire at 09:00 local (CT-204).
- reefer_monitor: end an excursion at the last reading received, marked not
  closed, when the logger goes quiet more than 15 minutes while out of range
  (CT-205).
- toll_allocation: ignore waived, $0.00 and zero-mile toll segments instead of
  rejecting the invoice run, so the remaining valid segments still allocate
  (CT-213).
- Fix EDI 997 overage comparison: the overage rate was always computed as zero,
  so acknowledgements exceeding the overage tolerance were reported as ACCEPTED
  instead of COUNT_MISMATCH (CT-207).

"""Regression coverage for TW-58213: the 14-hour window is exact whole minutes.

Replanning takes the clocks the ELD reports mid-shift, so the window left is
rarely a full 14 hours. Counting 59 minutes to the hour overstated it by a
minute for every 59, and a plan with a window that was really 600 minutes long
was allowed to drive past the close of the window instead of stopping for the
10-hour reset there.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from eta_planner import DriverClocks, estimate_arrival

DEPART = datetime(2026, 10, 12, 6, 0)
RESET = 10 * 60
WINDOW = 14 * 60


def test_tw_58213_no_driving_past_the_close_of_the_window():
    for window_left in (60, 200, 480, 520, 600, 601, 720, 840):
        for drive_minutes in (61, 200, 481, 571, 600, 660, 720, 1000, 1400):
            # 60 mph, so miles and driving minutes are the same number.
            plan = estimate_arrival(
                DEPART, drive_minutes, 60, DriverClocks(window_left=window_left)
            )
            closes = DEPART + timedelta(minutes=window_left)
            for kind, when in [*plan.stops, ("arrival", plan.arrival)]:
                assert when <= closes, (window_left, drive_minutes, kind)
                if kind == "reset":
                    closes = when + timedelta(minutes=RESET + WINDOW)

"""Location updates shared with customers during a load.

Carriers' ELDs report truck positions to us, and we pass a subset on to the
customer's tracking feed. Two limits apply. Positions are shared only while the
driver is on the customer's load, from pickup check-in to delivery check-out. And
updates are shared no more often than the minimum interval. ``share_schedule`` gives
the times the feed posts a position for a load; ``positions_to_share`` filters the
ELD pings down to what the customer may see.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

MIN_INTERVAL = timedelta(minutes=15)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Ping:
    at: datetime
    latitude: float
    longitude: float


def share_schedule(pickup_check_in: datetime, delivery_check_out: datetime, interval: timedelta = MIN_INTERVAL) -> list[datetime]:
    """Times to post a position, every ``interval`` from pickup check-in through check-out."""
    if interval < MIN_INTERVAL:
        raise ValueError(f"interval {interval} is shorter than the minimum {MIN_INTERVAL}")
    if delivery_check_out < pickup_check_in:
        raise ValueError("delivery check-out is before pickup check-in")
    times, current = [], pickup_check_in
    while current <= delivery_check_out:
        times.append(current)
        current += interval
    return times


def positions_to_share(pings: list[Ping], pickup_check_in: datetime, delivery_check_out: datetime, interval: timedelta = MIN_INTERVAL) -> list[Ping]:
    """The latest ping at or before each scheduled time, within the load window."""
    on_load = sorted((p for p in pings if pickup_check_in <= p.at <= delivery_check_out), key=lambda p: p.at)
    shared = []
    for slot in share_schedule(pickup_check_in, delivery_check_out, interval):
        latest = [p for p in on_load if p.at <= slot]
        if latest and (not shared or latest[-1] is not shared[-1]):
            shared.append(latest[-1])
    return shared

"""Cargo claim intake: is a loss and damage claim filed in time?

A customer whose freight arrived damaged, short, or not at all files a cargo
claim against the delivery. The claims desk screens each one before an adjuster
looks at it, and ``screen_claim`` is the first check: a claim filed after the
filing window has closed is denied as late. The window runs from the delivery
date (for a load never delivered, from the scheduled delivery date).
"""

import calendar
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

FILING_WINDOW_MONTHS = 9
ACCEPTED = "accepted"
DENIED_LATE = "denied_late"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Claim:
    claim_id: str
    customer: str
    delivered: date
    filed: date


def _add_months(start: date, months: int) -> date:
    """``start`` moved ``months`` months later, clamped to the end of a short month."""
    month_index = start.month - 1 + months
    year, month = start.year + month_index // 12, month_index % 12 + 1
    return date(year, month, min(start.day, calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]))


def filing_deadline(delivered: date) -> date:
    """The last day a claim on this delivery can be filed."""
    return _add_months(delivered, FILING_WINDOW_MONTHS)


def screen_claim(claim: Claim) -> str:
    if claim.filed < claim.delivered:
        raise ValueError(f"{claim.claim_id} filed before delivery")
    return ACCEPTED if claim.filed <= filing_deadline(claim.delivered) else DENIED_LATE

def test_excused_late_deliveries_are_excluded_from_the_denominator():

def test_excused_late_deliveries_do_not_dilute_the_measured_ratio():
    loads = [
        delivered("A", 0),
        delivered("B", 30),

        delivered("D", 90, code="CONS"),
